npcs.name: Loremaster Celarus
npcs.greet: Every question you ask me has been asked before, usually by someone more patient. Ask anyway. The asking is the lesson.

npcs.name: Ritemaster Iachesis
npcs.greet: Hm. You arrived exactly when I expected you, which is to say three days late. Sit. Time is a river, and we are about to go fishing.

relics.name: Mist-Pearl
relics.desc: A pale pearl that was in your hand when you woke. It is cool, faintly damp, and smells of sea fog.

relics.name: Shard of Frozen Time
relics.desc: A splinter of a breach between worlds. Raindrops hang motionless inside it.

relics.name: The Horologe of Kirenn
relics.desc: A Psijic instrument of nested silver rings that measures not hours but the distance between what is and what might have been.

ps_vision: The fog closes in. For a moment there is no ground under you, only grey, and the slow toll of a bell somewhere very far away.
We have watched you for longer than you have been watching yourself. Come west, to the isle that is not always there.
When the fog lifts, you are standing on a pale shore you have never seen, and an elf in a hooded robe is waiting as though you had an appointment.
ps_breach_sealed: Feel that? The world just exhaled. A breach is a wound where a moment that should never happen pushes into one that did.
The Daedra smell them, the way sharks smell blood. Someone is opening them on purpose. That is worse than any Daedra.
ps_ritemaster: Iachesis lifts the Horologe. Its rings spin until they blur, then stop, all at once, aligned. The torn air over Artaeum closes like an eye.
There. The isle is ours again. And the rite needed two pairs of hands, which I did not tell you, because you would have been nervous.
The Council has agreed. Few outsiders learn the Old Ways this quickly. Fewer still live long enough to teach them. Be the second kind.

quests.title: The Isle in the Mist
quests.offer: I keep dreaming of an island wrapped in fog.
quests.pitch: Then you are either mad or summoned, and I have met you, so I doubt you are mad. The Psijic Order calls people that way. Sail west, to where Artaeum ought to be, and if the isle wishes to be found, it will be.
quests.desc: For nights on end I dreamed of a fogbound island and a tolling bell. Magister Indaenir in Alinor told me it was a summons from the Psijic Order on Artaeum.

objectives.text: Sail west to the isle of Artaeum
Speak with the Psijic waiting on the shore
objectives.topic: I was dreaming of this place. Then I was here.
objectives.reply: Yes, that is generally how it goes. Keep the pearl; it was your invitation. Loremaster Celarus decides who stays. I only decide who gets lost on the way to him.

objectives.text: Show the Mist-Pearl to Loremaster Celarus
objectives.topic: Celinar says you decide who stays.
objectives.reply: I decide very little. The Order decided before you dreamed your first dream of us. But a pearl is only an invitation. Tell me why you came.

objectives.text: Answer Celarus

choices.label: To learn what the Mages Guild cannot teach.
choices.reply: Honest, and a little arrogant. The Guild teaches magic as a tool. We teach it as a conversation. You will find we argue back.

choices.label: Because the dream would not let me sleep.
choices.reply: Also honest. The Old Ways are not a choice so much as an itch. Welcome, Novice. Scratch carefully.

quests.outro: Artaeum let itself be found. Loremaster Celarus accepted me into the Psijic Order as a Novice, the first outsider in a long while.

consequence.summary: Artaeum let itself be found. Loremaster Celarus accepted me into the Psijic Order as a Novice, the first outsider in a long while.

quests.title: The Ceporah Trials
quests.pitch: Climb. Ceporah Tower stands on the western cliffs, and every Psijic has climbed it. Each floor tests a thing you think you are. Some come down different. A few come down quickly. Go when you are ready, which is now.
quests.desc: Loremaster Celarus sent me to Ceporah Tower, the ancient Psijic tower on Artaeum's cliffs, to face the trials every member of the Order has faced.

objectives.text: Climb to Ceporah Tower
Sit in silence on the first floor until the tower speaks
objectives.journal: The tower did not speak in words. It just grew quieter and quieter until I could hear my own doubts, one at a time.

objectives.text: Overcome the constructs of the second floor
Face the Warden of the Summit
objectives.journal: The Warden did not attack until I did. I wonder now whether I had to fight it at all.

objectives.text: Return to Loremaster Celarus
objectives.topic: I climbed the tower. Did I pass?
objectives.reply: You came down. That is the passing. The Warden would have let you by, if you had thought to ask. Most never do. Remember that, Initiate.

quests.outro: I faced the trials of Ceporah Tower. Celarus says the last of them could have been passed without a blow, and I am still thinking about that.

consequence.summary: I faced the trials of Ceporah Tower. Celarus says the last of them could have been passed without a blow, and I am still thinking about that.

quests.title: Breaches in Time
quests.pitch: Hands, and something sturdy attached to them. Tears are opening across Summerset, places where time has split and something has slipped in through the crack. Daedra, mostly. Close two for me, one near Firsthold and one outside Alinor. Bring me a shard.
quests.desc: Ritemaster Iachesis sent me to close breaches in time that have opened on Summerset and Auridon. Daedra are crawling through them.

objectives.text: Find the time breach outside Firsthold
Drive back the Daedra pouring through the breach
objectives.journal: Inside the breach, a moment kept repeating: the same gull, diving into the same wave, over and over. When the last Dremora fell, the gull finally caught its fish.

objectives.text: Find the second breach outside Alinor
Slay the Dremora holding the breach open
objectives.journal: Valzhar laughed as he died. He said the breach was not his doing, only his invitation.

objectives.text: Collect a shard of the collapsed breach
Bring the shard to Ritemaster Iachesis
objectives.topic: Both breaches are closed. One of the Dremora said he was invited.
objectives.reply: Was he. Then the shard will tell us by whom. Look at the raindrops in it. Each one is a moment that did not happen. Someone is fishing for one of them.

quests.outro: I closed two breaches in time and brought Iachesis a shard of one. The Dremora who held it claimed someone had opened the way on purpose.

consequence.summary: I closed two breaches in time and brought Iachesis a shard of one. The Dremora who held it claimed someone had opened the way on purpose.

quests.title: The Horologe of Kirenn
quests.desc: The breach shard pointed Iachesis to the Horologe of Kirenn, a Psijic instrument lost centuries ago. Sea Viper raiders from Pyandonea have found it in the ruins of Sunhold and are using it to tear holes in time.

objectives.text: Speak with Iachesis about the shard
objectives.topic: What did the shard tell you?
objectives.reply: A name. The Horologe of Kirenn, made by one of us before the Order left the world the first time. It measures the distance between what is and what might have been. In the wrong hands it shortens that distance. Maormer hands are very wrong. They hold Sunhold.

objectives.text: Travel to the ruins of Sunhold on Summerset
Break the Sea Viper hold on Sunhold
Defeat the Maormer tidecaller who wields the Horologe
objectives.journal: Sirathel wanted a moment in which Pyandonea had won the war against Summerset. She was close to finding it. The Horologe was warm in her hands when she fell.

objectives.text: Take the Horologe of Kirenn
Bring the Horologe to Loremaster Celarus on Artaeum
objectives.topic: The Maormer had it. They won't need it now.
objectives.reply: Kirenn's own work. I have read about this instrument since I was younger than you. Keep it a moment longer. Before it goes back to the vaults, you must understand what it measures.

quests.outro: I took the Horologe of Kirenn back from a Maormer tidecaller in the ruins of Sunhold. Celarus wants me to understand it before it is locked away.

consequence.summary: I took the Horologe of Kirenn back from a Maormer tidecaller in the ruins of Sunhold. Celarus wants me to understand it before it is locked away.

quests.title: The Old Ways
quests.desc: Celarus has agreed to teach me the Old Ways, the Psijic understanding of magic as a dialogue with the world rather than a command given to it.

objectives.text: Listen to Celarus's first lesson
objectives.reply: No one is. Listen. The Mages Guild says: I will make fire. The Old Ways say: there is fire here already, waiting to be asked. The difference sounds small. It is the width of the world.

objectives.text: Tell Celarus what you heard

choices.label: Then magic is listening, more than speaking.
choices.reply: Yes. And a mage who only speaks will one day be answered by something he did not expect.

choices.label: Then magic has a will of its own.
choices.reply: Not a will. A shape. Water has no will, but it has a shape it prefers. Learn the shape and you need never force it.

objectives.text: Go to the meditation stones below Ceporah Tower
Wait for the stars to rise over Artaeum
Confront the echo of the mage you might have been
objectives.journal: The echo cast every spell I know, louder than I cast them, and never once paused to see what the world answered. That was how I beat it.

objectives.text: Return to Celarus
objectives.topic: I met someone at the stones. Myself, more or less.
objectives.reply: The one who does not listen. Everyone meets theirs. Fewer get back up. You are an Adept of the Old Ways now, which means you have learned enough to know how little you know.

quests.outro: Celarus taught me the first of the Old Ways. Beneath Ceporah Tower, under the stars, I faced the mage I would have become without them.

consequence.summary: Celarus taught me the first of the Old Ways. Beneath Ceporah Tower, under the stars, I faced the mage I would have become without them.

quests.title: The Ritemaster's Rite
quests.desc: The Horologe has been used too many times. A breach has opened above Artaeum itself, and Iachesis must perform an old rite to close it while someone holds back what comes through.

objectives.text: Speak with Ritemaster Iachesis
objectives.topic: The sky over the isle is torn.
objectives.reply: Yes. Sirathel tugged at the threads too often, and they have unravelled here, where the Order's own past is thickest. I need the Horologe and I need time to work. You will give me the second one.

objectives.text: Hold back the Daedra while Iachesis works the rite
Slay the Markynaz who strides through the breach
objectives.journal: Ulvathar fought in three moments at once, his blade landing before it swung. I learned to strike where he would be rather than where he was.

objectives.text: Speak with Loremaster Celarus
objectives.topic: The breach is closed. Is the Horologe safe?
objectives.reply: In the vaults, where it will sleep until someone foolish wakes it again. Probably one of us. Take these, Loremaster. The circlet is old. The ones who wore it before you were not always wise, but they always listened.

quests.outro: Iachesis closed the breach over Artaeum while I held back the Daedra. The Council named me Loremaster of the Psijic Order, and one day, Iachesis says, I may stand where she stood.

consequence.summary: Iachesis closed the breach over Artaeum while I held back the Daedra. The Council named me Loremaster of the Psijic Order, and one day, Iachesis says, I may stand where she stood.
